- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by model overestimation, reduce peak by 5–10% to account for lagged market reaction.
- If forecast mean is consistently below true mean over 3–5 days, apply a 2–3% upward bias to reflect mean reversion toward recent highs.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3), reduce forecast smoothness and add 1–2% volatility buffer to avoid overfitting.
- If forecast consistently underestimates true price in 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 1–3% upward correction to reflect sentiment-driven breakout potential.
